title: Autopoiesis Of Society In The Medium Of Games

story.text: In what sense is society autopoietic, and why does Baecker propose “games” as the medium in which this autopoiesis occurs—especially in view of a possible “next society”?

Society can be described as an autopoietic system that reproduces itself in the medium of its **games**: structured forms of interaction that acquire recursive eigenvalue in a network, potentially pointing toward a “next society” organized as a network of games rather than by older differentiation forms.

support
Baecker takes up Maturana/Varela’s and Luhmann’s concept of autopoiesis but suspends commitments to particular differentiation forms (strata, center/periphery, function systems). Instead, he focuses on which “games” within this autopoiesis gain recursive weight.

support
He hints that with electricity, computers and the internet, it might be more fruitful to think in terms of a “next society” whose differentiation form is networks of games, rather than function systems. Flow metaphors and game participation across contexts suggest a new culture form succeeding boundary, telos, and restless equilibria.

support
Games are where observers encounter each other under rules, frames, and meta-frames (Bateson). They are privileged sites where Widerstreit is staged, where Negativsprachen and Positivsprachen intertwine, and where cultural symbols and media can be experimented with.

oppose
Skeptics may say that “games” risk trivializing serious asymmetries of power, coercion, and exclusion; not every social arena in which people “play along” is best described as game rather than as constraint or domination.

oppose
Another objection: shifting from function systems to games and networks might underplay the continuing force of institutionalized differentiation (law, science, politics, economy) that still structures which games can be played and who is allowed to join.
